builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Follow the Entities: A Corpus Map for Agentic Search
summary: CorpusMap replaces repeated per-query rediscovery of cross-document relationships in agentic search with an offline-built graph of entity pages that aggregate mentions and link to all referencing documents. It costs an offline entity-resolution and indexing pipeline over the corpus, ongoing maintenance as documents change, and added prompt/context structure for the agent to traverse the graph. It can fail when entity resolution produces incorrect merges or splits, when queries involve entities not recurring enough to have pages, or when corpus updates leave the offline index stale relative to the documents.
rationale: The approach is feasible on constrained infrastructure since it requires only offline indexing plus API-based agents, but the claimed quality and token gains are unquantified in the abstract and depend on corpus entity density and resolution quality, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot before production adoption.
technique: Entity-centric corpus navigation layer for agentic search

claims.statement: CorpusMap replaces repeated per-query rediscovery of cross-document relationships in agentic search with an offline-built graph of entity pages that aggregate mentions and link to all referencing documents. It costs an offline entity-resolution and indexing pipeline over the corpus, ongoing maintenance as documents change, and added prompt/context structure for the agent to traverse the graph. It can fail when entity resolution produces incorrect merges or splits, when queries involve entities not recurring enough to have pages, or when corpus updates leave the offline index stale relative to the documents.

Improves evidence discovery and answer quality over raw-corpus agentic search while using fewer tokens on average, and outperforms 4 alternative navigation layers across 7 models and 3 benchmarks; no quantified figures given in the abstract.
